inputs.original_text: A South Portland parent of three is apologizing to school staff as they face another budget shortfall and cuts of more than 70 positions. That shouldn’t be treated as an unavoidable accounting problem: when public schools are chronically underfunded, workers are made to carry the strain and students risk losing the support they need. Educators and school staff deserve decent conditions, and children shouldn’t pay the price for institutions failing to invest in them.
inputs.modified_text: A South Portland parent of three is apologizing to school staff as another budget shortfall threatens more than 70 positions. That apology says a lot about how families are left to absorb the guilt and worry created by chronic underinvestment. These cuts aren’t just numbers: they put workers’ livelihoods and students’ access to support at risk. Schools need sustained public investment, not a system that makes staff and children bear the cost of institutional failure.
